title: Iterative prefetch and fine-grained timeboxing for rerank endpoint to reduce tail latency
creator: Ariana Chen
description:
Problem: The reranking endpoint exhibits high tail latency under mixed traffic: long candidate lists (100-1000 items), a wide token length distribution, and concurrent requests with varying deadlines. Existing continuous batching reduces CPU/GPU cost but compounds tail latency because large batches wait for slow candidates and single-request deadlines are coarse-grained.

Goal: Implement an iterative prefetch + fine-grained timeboxing strategy that parallelizes candidate scoring across multiple worker shards, enforces per-candidate token quotas, and applies cascading soft deadlines so slow candidates do not block short-deadline requests. The solution should be compatible with KV cache reuse and not regress throughput or accuracy beyond configurable tolerances.

Scope: Design + implementation in rerank service, unit and perf tests, canary rollout, and monitoring. Non-goals: model architecture changes or full rewrite of scheduler logic for other endpoints (chat/generation).
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile latency for 1k-candidate rerank requests decreases by >=30% under production-like mixed load
P99 latency decreases by >=20% for median request sizes (50-200 candidates)
End-to-end quality (Spearman rho on held-out eval set) does not drop more than 1% compared to baseline unless the policy explicitly truncates candidates (configurable per-route)
No increase in per-token CPU time more than 10% at 95th percentile when running steady-state throughput
Feature gated and controlled rollout with automatic fallback to current scheduler on errors or SLO violation
implementation_notes:
Design components: 1) Iterative prefetcher: stream candidate score work to N worker shards; prefetch KV cache entries per shard in parallel before scoring. 2) Per-candidate token quota: cap compute for extremely long inputs (configurable percentiles), emit partial scores with provenance. 3) Timeboxing: soft deadlines applied at shard and request level; implement cascading eviction of low-priority candidates when shard deadline is hit. 4) Sparse parallelization: for small candidate counts run single-shard path to avoid overhead; for large lists spawn controlled parallelism. 5) Telemetry: per-candidate timing, kv-hit/miss, prefetch latency, bytes fetched.

Key design trade-offs recorded: parallelism reduces tail but adds KV cache contention; mitigated by prefetching and token quotas. We will introduce a new route-level config with defaults tuned from dist-1000 workload.

Testing plan: microbenchmarks with synthetic candidate length distributions, integration perf runs against canary cluster, rollout to 10% traffic then 50% with SLO gating.

Rollout: feature-flagged behind rerank.parallel_prefetch and rerank.fine_timeboxing; start with simulation mode -> shadow scoring -> canary traffic -> full rollout.
